'''John C. Crocker''' (born 1968 in [[Stoughton, Massachusetts]]) is an American [[physicist]] and [[chemical engineer]]. He is a Professor of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref name=SEAS>{{Cite web|url=https://directory.engineering.upenn.edu/john-c-crocker/|title=John C. Crocker}}</ref>

Crocker's research is focused in [[soft matter physics]], [[nanotechnology]] and [[cell mechanics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=NLH31KIAAAAJ&hl=en|title=John C Crocker|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

==Education==
Crocker studied Physics at the [[University of Chicago]], graduating with an AB in Physics in 1990. He continued his graduate studies at the University of Chicago and completed this program in 1996, receiving AM and PhD degrees in Physics, under the supervision of [[David G. Grier]]. This was followed by postdoctoral study with [[Arjun G. Yodh]] and [[David A. Weitz]] at the [[University of Pennsylvania]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.engineering.upenn.edu/~jcrocker/JCCshort.pdf|title=John Charles Crocker}}</ref>

==Career==
In 2000, following his postdoctoral work, Crocker was appointed as Assistant Professor in Applied Physics at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. In 2001, he moved to become Skirkanich Assistant Professor of Innovation in Chemical and Biomolecular engineering at the University of Pennsylvania. Crocker was promoted to Associate Professor in 2007, and full Professor in 2014.<ref name=SEAS/>

==Research==
Crocker is known for his early work on [[Single-particle tracking|particle tracking]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.physics.emory.edu/faculty/weeks//idl/|title=Particle tracking using IDL|website=www.physics.emory.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://site.physics.georgetown.edu/matlab/|title=Matlab Particle Tracking|website=site.physics.georgetown.edu}}</ref> in two- and three-dimensions,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://soft-matter.github.io/trackpy/v0.4.2/|title=Trackpy: Fast, Flexible Particle-Tracking Toolkit — trackpy 0.4.2 documentation|website=soft-matter.github.io}}</ref> and the measurement of small forces between [[colloidal]] micro particles using [[optical tweezers]].<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.4870806|title=A tunable line optical tweezers instrument with nanometer spatial resolution|first1=W. Benjamin|last1=Rogers|first2=John C.|last2=Crocker|date=April 1, 2014|journal=Review of Scientific Instruments|volume=85|issue=4|page=043704|via=aip.scitation.org (Atypon)|doi=10.1063/1.4870806|pmid=24784615|bibcode=2014RScI...85d3704R |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His other significant work includes the development of [[Microrheology|two-point microrheology]]<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.888|title=Two-Point Microrheology of Inhomogeneous Soft Materials|first1=John C.|last1=Crocker|first2=M. T.|last2=Valentine|first3=Eric R.|last3=Weeks|first4=T.|last4=Gisler|first5=P. D.|last5=Kaplan|first6=A. G.|last6=Yodh|first7=D. A.|last7=Weitz|date=July 24, 2000|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=85|issue=4|pages=888–891|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.888|pmid=10991424|bibcode=2000PhRvL..85..888C |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and its application to cell mechanics and force spectrum microscopy measurements, as well as the use of DNA hybridization to direct the formation of novel [[colloidal crystals]].<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.058302|title=Colloidal Interactions and Self-Assembly Using DNA Hybridization|first1=Paul L.|last1=Biancaniello|first2=Anthony J.|last2=Kim|first3=John C.|last3=Crocker|date=February 10, 2005|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=94|issue=5|article-number=058302|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.058302|pmid=15783705|bibcode=2005PhRvL..94e8302B |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His later work involves the use of energy landscape methods to understanding soft glassy materials, such as foams and the actomyosin cytoskeleton.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nmat4663|title=Understanding soft glassy materials using an energy landscape approach|first1=Hyun Joo|last1=Hwang|first2=Robert A.|last2=Riggleman|first3=John C.|last3=Crocker|date=September 17, 2016|journal=Nature Materials|volume=15|issue=9|pages=1031–1036|via=www.nature.com|doi=10.1038/nmat4663|pmid=27322823|bibcode=2016NatMa..15.1031H |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

*2002 - Fellow of the [[David & Lucile Packard Foundation]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.packard.org/what-we-fund/science/packard-fellowships-for-science-and-engineering/fellowship-directory/crocker-john-c/|title=Crocker, John C.}}</ref>
*2005 - "Brilliant 10", [[Popular Science]] Magazine<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.popsci.com/scitech/article/2006-07/popscis-fourth-annual-brilliant-10/|title=PopSci's Fourth Annual Brilliant 10|website=Popular Science}}</ref>
*2018 - Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org}}</ref>
